content.content:
# How to File Things

Read this before you put anything on this drive.

---

## Why filing feels hard

You have been sorting by subject. Every file has several subjects at once, so
several folders are always "correct," and you stall. A finished football GPS
report is about football, about GPS, about reporting, and about the 2026 season.
Four folders all look right, so it stays in the inbox.

The fix is to stop sorting by subject.

---

## The one principle

**The folder answers "what stage is this in." The filename answers "what is it about."**

A file has many subjects but only one stage at a time. Stage has exactly one
right answer, so there is nothing to decide.

Sport, season, vendor, and topic all go in the filename. They are never the
reason you pick a folder.

---

## The ladder

Ask these in order. Stop at the first yes. That is the folder.

**1. Am I still working on it?**
   `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/YYYY-MM-DD_ProjectName/`
   Drafts, data pulls, scratch notes, code, half-built decks. If the work is not
   done, everything about it lives in the project folder, no matter what type of
   file it is.

**2. Is it finished, and did I hand it to someone or will I?**
   `03_REPORTS/`
   The final PDF. The deck you presented. The annual report you submitted. One
   file per deliverable. This is the folder you search when someone asks "what
   did we send them in October."

**3. Is it a blank I reuse to make other things?**
   `06_TEMPLATES/`
   Empty intake forms, report shells, protocol documents, checklists. If it has
   real athlete data in it, it is not a template.

**4. Is it about a tool or vendor rather than about athletes?**
   `05_SYSTEMS/<Vendor>/`
   Contracts, API docs, setup guides, vendor whitepapers, license paperwork.
   Catapult, Vald, Hawkin, PFF, Power BI, Claude.

**5. Is it standing operational material for one sport and season?**
   `02_SPORTS/<Sport>/<Season>/`
   Rosters, practice schedules, travel itineraries, team calendars. Only the
   recurring stuff you rebuild every season. Not projects, not reports.

**6. Is it for my own growth rather than my job's output?**
   `09_PRO_DEV/`
   Courses, certifications, conference recordings, books, other people's
   research papers.

**7. Is it administrative?**
   `08_ADMIN/`
   Meeting notes and transcripts, personnel, policy, equipment, budgets.

**8. None of the above, and it is done?**
   `10_ARCHIVE/YYYY/`

If you get past 8, you did not need the file.

---

## The hard cases, decided in advance

These are the ones that actually stall you. The answers are fixed so you do not
have to think about them again.

| Thing | Where it goes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Annual report, while you are writing it | `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` | Rung 1 beats rung 2 |
| Annual report, the final submitted PDF | `03_REPORTS/` | It shipped |
| The eight in-between drafts | Delete, or `_old/` inside the project | Not deliverables |
| A deck you built and presented once | `03_REPORTS/` | You handed it to someone |
| A deck you present every year to interns | `07_EDUCATION/` | It is curriculum, you reuse it |
| CMJ traffic light app code | `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` | It is a project that happens to be about volleyball |
| Volleyball roster for FA2026 | `02_SPORTS/Volleyball/FA2026/` | Standing seasonal material |
| Hawkin SaaS agreement | `05_SYSTEMS/Hawkin/` | Vendor paperwork |
| A research paper someone else wrote | `09_PRO_DEV/` | Not your output |
| A study you are running | `04_RESEARCH/` | Your output, ongoing |
| Fireflies transcript of a staff meeting | `08_ADMIN/` | Administrative |
| Raw GPS export you pulled for one analysis | Inside that project folder | It belongs to the analysis |
| Anything personal | Not on this drive | It is a Baylor account |

**The tiebreaker for everything else:** if two rungs both seem right, the lower
number wins. The ladder is ordered on purpose.

---

## Naming

Three rules. Apply them to new files only. Do not go back and rename 43,000
old ones.

**1. Date first, if the thing is tied to a moment in time.**
   `2026-08-18_` at the front. Year first means it sorts correctly forever.
   Use the date it was finished, not the date you last opened it.

**2. Subject tag second.**
   `FB_`, `VB_`, `WBB_`, `MBB_`, `SOC_`, `SB_`. Season codes are `FA2026`,
   `SP2026`, `SUM2026`. Four-digit year, always. Never `FA25`.

**3. Underscores, not spaces. No apostrophes. No parentheses.**

Put together: `2026-08-18_FB_GPS_WeeklyReport_v2.pdf`

**Words that are banned in anything you intend to keep:**
`final_final`, `Copy of`, `New`, `Old`, `temp`, `USE THIS`, `v2 (1)`.
Every one of those means you already lost track of which copy is current.

---

## Killing redundancy

**One home.** A file lives in exactly one folder. If it truly belongs in two,
put it in the lower-numbered one and make a Windows shortcut in the other. Never
copy.

**One current version.** When you save `_v2`, delete `_v1` or move it into an
`_old/` folder inside the project. The project folder is allowed to be messy.
Nothing above rung 1 is.

**When you find three copies of the same file,** keep the one in `03_REPORTS`
or `10_ARCHIVE`. Those are the folders that are supposed to be permanent.
Delete the rest.

**Never keep both the .docx and the .pdf of a finished deliverable in
`03_REPORTS`.** Keep the PDF there. The .docx stays with the project.

---

## The two habits

Everything above fails without these. They are the whole system.

**1. Friday, 15 minutes: inbox to zero.**
Open `00_INBOX`. Run every file down the ladder. File it or delete it. The
inbox is a landing strip, not a hangar. Nothing sleeps there over the weekend.

**2. When something ships, it moves that day.**
The moment you send a report, move the final out of `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` into
`03_REPORTS/`, and move the project folder into `_DONE/`. Do it while you still
remember which file was the real one. A week later you will not.

At year end, `_DONE/` empties into `10_ARCHIVE/YYYY/`. That takes about ten
minutes once a year.

---

## What "done" looks like

- `00_INBOX` is empty most days.
- `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE` holds fewer than ten folders. If it holds thirty, most
  of them are actually stalled, and they should say so.
- You can find any finished deliverable from the last three years by opening
  `03_REPORTS` and sorting by name, because the dates are in front.
- You never think about where a file goes. You run the ladder and stop at the
  first yes.
=====MAP=====
# Migration Map

Created 2026-08-18. The new empty folders are in place. **Nothing has moved yet.**

Until the moves run, the drive has two structures side by side. That is
temporary and intentional, so you can look at the target before committing to
it. Work down this table when you are ready.

---

## Old folder to new folder

| Old | New | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `00_INBOX\DEV\*` | `01_PROJECTS\_ACTIVE\` | 13 projects. Rename each with a `YYYY-MM-DD_` prefix as it moves. This is the big one. |
| `01_ACTIVE_PROJECTS\01_ONGOING` | `01_PROJECTS\_ACTIVE\` | 3 loose .docx files here need homes, not just the folders |
| `01_ACTIVE_PROJECTS\02_STALLED` | `01_PROJECTS\_STALLED\` | Straight move |
| `01_ACTIVE_PROJECTS\00_ARCHIVE` | `01_PROJECTS\_DONE\` | Then sort into `10_ARCHIVE\YYYY\` by finish year |
| `02_BAIR_RESEARCH` | `04_RESEARCH\` | Straight move |
| `03_SPORTS_PROGRAMS` | `02_SPORTS\` | Only Football, Volleyball, Cheer, Acrobatics_Tumbling have content. The other 10 are empty, do not recreate them. |
| `04_REPORTS_DELIVERABLES` | `03_REPORTS\` | Flatten `DEPARTMENT`, `TEAM`, `TECHNOLOGY`, `SPECIAL REQUEST` into one level, tag in filenames instead |
| `05_DATA_SYSTEMS` | `05_SYSTEMS\` | Drop the 4 empty vendor folders |
| `05_TEMPLATES_PROTOCOLS` | `06_TEMPLATES\` | Fixes the duplicate 05 prefix |
| `06_MEETINGS_ADMIN` | `08_ADMIN\` | Straight move |
| `07_EDUCATION_TEACHING` | `07_EDUCATION\` | Straight move |
| `08_ARCHIVE\2023`, `\2024`, `\2026` | `10_ARCHIVE\YYYY\` | 2023 and 2024 are empty |
| `08_ARCHIVE\PERSONAL` | **Off this drive** | Family, finance, home inspection, billing. Move to personal storage. |
| `09_PROFESSIONAL_DEVELOPMENT` | `09_PRO_DEV\` | 34 GB, mostly conference video. Consider offloading the .mp4 files to external storage. |
| `10_HEALTH_AND_WELLNESS` | Split | `TEAM_EDUCATION` to `07_EDUCATION`, finished pieces to `03_REPORTS`, the rest to `10_ARCHIVE` |
| `11_AI_RESEARCH` | `05_SYSTEMS\Claude\` | 14 files, duplicates what is already in `05_DATA_SYSTEMS\Claude` |
| `XX_MIGRATION` | `99_UNSORTED\` | 97.7 GB. Do not sort it. See below. |
| `XXXX_Transfer` | `05_SYSTEMS\` | 19 files of software docs |

---

## What NOT to do

**Do not try to sort `99_UNSORTED`.** It holds 20,827 files and you touched 172
of them in the last year. Refiling it would take days and buy you almost
nothing. Instead, pull out only these four, which you will actually reach for:

- `From_Desktop\CodingProjects`
- `From_External\Performance Play Book`
- `From_External\Policy`
- `From_GPS_Laptop\GPS REPORTS`

Leave the rest sitting there. Windows Search will find a 2014 PDF faster than
you will refile it. Revisit the whole folder on 2027-01-01 and delete what you
still have not opened.

**Do not recreate empty folders.** Sport folders, vendor folders, and archive
year folders get created the moment something goes in them, not before. Empty
scaffolding is what taught you to stop looking in `03_SPORTS_PROGRAMS`.

---

## Before any of this: two things that are not organizing

These matter more than the folder moves and take about an hour together.

**1. Rotate the exposed credentials.** Seven plain-text key files plus five
`.env` files are syncing to a Baylor-managed cloud drive. One has the key value
in the filename, so it shows up in search results and share previews. Rotate
the keys, delete the files, move the secrets to a password manager or Windows
environment variables.

**2. Get code out of OneDrive.** 94,722 of your files are `node_modules`,
`venv`, `.git`, and `site-packages`. Move code projects to a local path like
`C:\dev\` and they stop syncing. That removes about 95,000 files and 4 GB, and
every folder in Explorer gets faster.

---

## Suggested order

1. Rotate credentials, delete the key files
2. Move code projects out of OneDrive to `C:\dev\`
3. Delete the 771 empty folders
4. Move `00_INBOX\DEV\*` into `01_PROJECTS\_ACTIVE\` with date prefixes
5. Run the straight moves in the table above
6. Rename `XX_MIGRATION` to `99_UNSORTED`, pull the four folders worth keeping
7. Move personal material off the Baylor drive
8. Delete the old empty top-level folders once they are drained
9. Start the Friday inbox habit
=====od_to_gdrive=====
# od_to_gdrive.ps1 -- copy OneDrive primary drive folders to Google Drive, verify, then move originals to _MIGRATED_to_GoogleDrive
param([string]$FolderList)
$Folders = $FolderList -split ','
$src = 'C:\Users\eric_rash\OneDrive - Baylor University\00_Primary_Storage_Drive'
$dst = 'G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive'
$done = "$src\_MIGRATED_to_GoogleDrive"
$log = "C:\DEV\_tools\od_migrate_log_$(Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd_HHmm).txt"
function L($m){ "$(Get-Date -Format HH:mm:ss) $m" | Tee-Object -FilePath $log -Append }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $done | Out-Null
L "START folders: $($Folders -join ', ')"
foreach ($f in $Folders) {
  $s = Join-Path $src $f; $d = Join-Path $dst $f
  if (-not (Test-Path $s)) { L "SKIP $f (not found)"; continue }
  L "== $f : copying"
  robocopy $s $d /E /COPY:DT /DCOPY:T /R:2 /W:5 /NP /NFL /NDL /NJH /XJ /LOG+:"$log.robocopy.txt" | Out-Null
  $rc = $LASTEXITCODE
  $srcCount = (Get-ChildItem $s -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object).Count
  $dstCount = (Get-ChildItem $d -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object).Count
  if ($rc -lt 8 -and $dstCount -ge $srcCount) {
    Move-Item $s "$done\$f" -Force
    L "   OK  $f : $srcCount files copied, original moved to _MIGRATED_to_GoogleDrive (robocopy rc=$rc)"
  } else {
    L "   !! $f : NOT moved. robocopy rc=$rc, src=$srcCount dst=$dstCount. Re-run this folder later."
  }
}
# loose root files
foreach ($lf in (Get-ChildItem $src -File)) {
  Copy-Item $lf.FullName $dst -Force
  if (Test-Path (Join-Path $dst $lf.Name)) { Move-Item $lf.FullName "$done\" -Force; L "   OK  root file $($lf.Name)" }
}
L "DONE"
=====od_queue_big3=====
# wait for the running migration to finish, then migrate the three large folders
$logdir = 'C:\DEV\_tools'
do {
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 60
  $latest = Get-ChildItem "$logdir\od_migrate_log_*.txt" | Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch 'robocopy' } | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
  $finished = $latest -and (Select-String -Path $latest.FullName -Pattern '^\S+ DONE' -Quiet)
} until ($finished)
& "$logdir\od_to_gdrive.ps1" -FolderList "08_ARCHIVE,09_PRO_DEV,99_UNSORTED"

# How to File Things

Read this before you put anything on this drive.

---

## Why filing feels hard

You have been sorting by subject. Every file has several subjects at once, so
several folders are always "correct," and you stall. A finished football GPS
report is about football, about GPS, about reporting, and about the 2026 season.
Four folders all look right, so it stays in the inbox.

The fix is to stop sorting by subject.

---

## The one principle

**The folder answers "what stage is this in." The filename answers "what is it about."**

A file has many subjects but only one stage at a time. Stage has exactly one
right answer, so there is nothing to decide.

Sport, season, vendor, and topic all go in the filename. They are never the
reason you pick a folder.

---

## The ladder

Ask these in order. Stop at the first yes. That is the folder.

**1. Am I still working on it?**
   `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/YYYY-MM-DD_ProjectName/`
   Drafts, data pulls, scratch notes, code, half-built decks. If the work is not
   done, everything about it lives in the project folder, no matter what type of
   file it is.

**2. Is it finished, and did I hand it to someone or will I?**
   `03_REPORTS/`
   The final PDF. The deck you presented. The annual report you submitted. One
   file per deliverable. This is the folder you search when someone asks "what
   did we send them in October."

**3. Is it a blank I reuse to make other things?**
   `06_TEMPLATES/`
   Empty intake forms, report shells, protocol documents, checklists. If it has
   real athlete data in it, it is not a template.

**4. Is it about a tool or vendor rather than about athletes?**
   `05_SYSTEMS/<Vendor>/`
   Contracts, API docs, setup guides, vendor whitepapers, license paperwork.
   Catapult, Vald, Hawkin, PFF, Power BI, Claude.

**5. Is it standing operational material for one sport and season?**
   `02_SPORTS/<Sport>/<Season>/`
   Rosters, practice schedules, travel itineraries, team calendars. Only the
   recurring stuff you rebuild every season. Not projects, not reports.

**6. Is it for my own growth rather than my job's output?**
   `09_PRO_DEV/`
   Courses, certifications, conference recordings, books, other people's
   research papers.

**7. Is it administrative?**
   `08_ADMIN/`
   Meeting notes and transcripts, personnel, policy, equipment, budgets.

**8. None of the above, and it is done?**
   `10_ARCHIVE/YYYY/`

If you get past 8, you did not need the file.

---

## The hard cases, decided in advance

These are the ones that actually stall you. The answers are fixed so you do not
have to think about them again.

| Thing | Where it goes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Annual report, while you are writing it | `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` | Rung 1 beats rung 2 |
| Annual report, the final submitted PDF | `03_REPORTS/` | It shipped |
| The eight in-between drafts | Delete, or `_old/` inside the project | Not deliverables |
| A deck you built and presented once | `03_REPORTS/` | You handed it to someone |
| A deck you present every year to interns | `07_EDUCATION/` | It is curriculum, you reuse it |
| CMJ traffic light app code | `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` | It is a project that happens to be about volleyball |
| Volleyball roster for FA2026 | `02_SPORTS/Volleyball/FA2026/` | Standing seasonal material |
| Hawkin SaaS agreement | `05_SYSTEMS/Hawkin/` | Vendor paperwork |
| A research paper someone else wrote | `09_PRO_DEV/` | Not your output |
| A study you are running | `04_RESEARCH/` | Your output, ongoing |
| Fireflies transcript of a staff meeting | `08_ADMIN/` | Administrative |
| Raw GPS export you pulled for one analysis | Inside that project folder | It belongs to the analysis |
| Anything personal | Not on this drive | It is a Baylor account |

**The tiebreaker for everything else:** if two rungs both seem right, the lower
number wins. The ladder is ordered on purpose.

---

## Naming

Three rules. Apply them to new files only. Do not go back and rename 43,000
old ones.

**1. Date first, if the thing is tied to a moment in time.**
   `2026-08-18_` at the front. Year first means it sorts correctly forever.
   Use the date it was finished, not the date you last opened it.

**2. Subject tag second.**
   `FB_`, `VB_`, `WBB_`, `MBB_`, `SOC_`, `SB_`. Season codes are `FA2026`,
   `SP2026`, `SUM2026`. Four-digit year, always. Never `FA25`.

**3. Underscores, not spaces. No apostrophes. No parentheses.**

Put together: `2026-08-18_FB_GPS_WeeklyReport_v2.pdf`

**Words that are banned in anything you intend to keep:**
`final_final`, `Copy of`, `New`, `Old`, `temp`, `USE THIS`, `v2 (1)`.
Every one of those means you already lost track of which copy is current.

---

## Killing redundancy

**One home.** A file lives in exactly one folder. If it truly belongs in two,
put it in the lower-numbered one and make a Windows shortcut in the other. Never
copy.

**One current version.** When you save `_v2`, delete `_v1` or move it into an
`_old/` folder inside the project. The project folder is allowed to be messy.
Nothing above rung 1 is.

**When you find three copies of the same file,** keep the one in `03_REPORTS`
or `10_ARCHIVE`. Those are the folders that are supposed to be permanent.
Delete the rest.

**Never keep both the .docx and the .pdf of a finished deliverable in
`03_REPORTS`.** Keep the PDF there. The .docx stays with the project.

---

## The two habits

Everything above fails without these. They are the whole system.

**1. Friday, 15 minutes: inbox to zero.**
Open `00_INBOX`. Run every file down the ladder. File it or delete it. The
inbox is a landing strip, not a hangar. Nothing sleeps there over the weekend.

**2. When something ships, it moves that day.**
The moment you send a report, move the final out of `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` into
`03_REPORTS/`, and move the project folder into `_DONE/`. Do it while you still
remember which file was the real one. A week later you will not.

At year end, `_DONE/` empties into `10_ARCHIVE/YYYY/`. That takes about ten
minutes once a year.

---

## What "done" looks like

- `00_INBOX` is empty most days.
- `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE` holds fewer than ten folders. If it holds thirty, most
  of them are actually stalled, and they should say so.
- You can find any finished deliverable from the last three years by opening
  `03_REPORTS` and sorting by name, because the dates are in front.
- You never think about where a file goes. You run the ladder and stop at the
  first yes.
=====MAP=====
# Migration Map

Created 2026-08-18. The new empty folders are in place. **Nothing has moved yet.**

Until the moves run, the drive has two structures side by side. That is
temporary and intentional, so you can look at the target before committing to
it. Work down this table when you are ready.

---

## Old folder to new folder

| Old | New | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `00_INBOX\DEV\*` | `01_PROJECTS\_ACTIVE\` | 13 projects. Rename each with a `YYYY-MM-DD_` prefix as it moves. This is the big one. |
| `01_ACTIVE_PROJECTS\01_ONGOING` | `01_PROJECTS\_ACTIVE\` | 3 loose .docx files here need homes, not just the folders |
| `01_ACTIVE_PROJECTS\02_STALLED` | `01_PROJECTS\_STALLED\` | Straight move |
| `01_ACTIVE_PROJECTS\00_ARCHIVE` | `01_PROJECTS\_DONE\` | Then sort into `10_ARCHIVE\YYYY\` by finish year |
| `02_BAIR_RESEARCH` | `04_RESEARCH\` | Straight move |
| `03_SPORTS_PROGRAMS` | `02_SPORTS\` | Only Football, Volleyball, Cheer, Acrobatics_Tumbling have content. The other 10 are empty, do not recreate them. |
| `04_REPORTS_DELIVERABLES` | `03_REPORTS\` | Flatten `DEPARTMENT`, `TEAM`, `TECHNOLOGY`, `SPECIAL REQUEST` into one level, tag in filenames instead |
| `05_DATA_SYSTEMS` | `05_SYSTEMS\` | Drop the 4 empty vendor folders |
| `05_TEMPLATES_PROTOCOLS` | `06_TEMPLATES\` | Fixes the duplicate 05 prefix |
| `06_MEETINGS_ADMIN` | `08_ADMIN\` | Straight move |
| `07_EDUCATION_TEACHING` | `07_EDUCATION\` | Straight move |
| `08_ARCHIVE\2023`, `\2024`, `\2026` | `10_ARCHIVE\YYYY\` | 2023 and 2024 are empty |
| `08_ARCHIVE\PERSONAL` | **Off this drive** | Family, finance, home inspection, billing. Move to personal storage. |
| `09_PROFESSIONAL_DEVELOPMENT` | `09_PRO_DEV\` | 34 GB, mostly conference video. Consider offloading the .mp4 files to external storage. |
| `10_HEALTH_AND_WELLNESS` | Split | `TEAM_EDUCATION` to `07_EDUCATION`, finished pieces to `03_REPORTS`, the rest to `10_ARCHIVE` |
| `11_AI_RESEARCH` | `05_SYSTEMS\Claude\` | 14 files, duplicates what is already in `05_DATA_SYSTEMS\Claude` |
| `XX_MIGRATION` | `99_UNSORTED\` | 97.7 GB. Do not sort it. See below. |
| `XXXX_Transfer` | `05_SYSTEMS\` | 19 files of software docs |

---

## What NOT to do

**Do not try to sort `99_UNSORTED`.** It holds 20,827 files and you touched 172
of them in the last year. Refiling it would take days and buy you almost
nothing. Instead, pull out only these four, which you will actually reach for:

- `From_Desktop\CodingProjects`
- `From_External\Performance Play Book`
- `From_External\Policy`
- `From_GPS_Laptop\GPS REPORTS`

Leave the rest sitting there. Windows Search will find a 2014 PDF faster than
you will refile it. Revisit the whole folder on 2027-01-01 and delete what you
still have not opened.

**Do not recreate empty folders.** Sport folders, vendor folders, and archive
year folders get created the moment something goes in them, not before. Empty
scaffolding is what taught you to stop looking in `03_SPORTS_PROGRAMS`.

---

## Before any of this: two things that are not organizing

These matter more than the folder moves and take about an hour together.

**1. Rotate the exposed credentials.** Seven plain-text key files plus five
`.env` files are syncing to a Baylor-managed cloud drive. One has the key value
in the filename, so it shows up in search results and share previews. Rotate
the keys, delete the files, move the secrets to a password manager or Windows
environment variables.

**2. Get code out of OneDrive.** 94,722 of your files are `node_modules`,
`venv`, `.git`, and `site-packages`. Move code projects to a local path like
`C:\dev\` and they stop syncing. That removes about 95,000 files and 4 GB, and
every folder in Explorer gets faster.

---

## Suggested order

1. Rotate credentials, delete the key files
2. Move code projects out of OneDrive to `C:\dev\`
3. Delete the 771 empty folders
4. Move `00_INBOX\DEV\*` into `01_PROJECTS\_ACTIVE\` with date prefixes
5. Run the straight moves in the table above
6. Rename `XX_MIGRATION` to `99_UNSORTED`, pull the four folders worth keeping
7. Move personal material off the Baylor drive
8. Delete the old empty top-level folders once they are drained
9. Start the Friday inbox habit

# od_to_gdrive.ps1 -- copy OneDrive primary drive folders to Google Drive, verify, then move originals to _MIGRATED_to_GoogleDrive
param([string]$FolderList)
$Folders = $FolderList -split ','
$src = 'C:\Users\eric_rash\OneDrive - Baylor University\00_Primary_Storage_Drive'
$dst = 'G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive'
$done = "$src\_MIGRATED_to_GoogleDrive"
$log = "C:\DEV\_tools\od_migrate_log_$(Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd_HHmm).txt"
function L($m){ "$(Get-Date -Format HH:mm:ss) $m" | Tee-Object -FilePath $log -Append }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $done | Out-Null
L "START folders: $($Folders -join ', ')"
foreach ($f in $Folders) {
  $s = Join-Path $src $f; $d = Join-Path $dst $f
  if (-not (Test-Path $s)) { L "SKIP $f (not found)"; continue }
  L "== $f : copying"
  robocopy $s $d /E /COPY:DT /DCOPY:T /R:2 /W:5 /NP /NFL /NDL /NJH /XJ /LOG+:"$log.robocopy.txt" | Out-Null
  $rc = $LASTEXITCODE
  $srcCount = (Get-ChildItem $s -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object).Count
  $dstCount = (Get-ChildItem $d -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object).Count
  if ($rc -lt 8 -and $dstCount -ge $srcCount) {
    Move-Item $s "$done\$f" -Force
    L "   OK  $f : $srcCount files copied, original moved to _MIGRATED_to_GoogleDrive (robocopy rc=$rc)"
  } else {
    L "   !! $f : NOT moved. robocopy rc=$rc, src=$srcCount dst=$dstCount. Re-run this folder later."
  }
}
# loose root files
foreach ($lf in (Get-ChildItem $src -File)) {
  Copy-Item $lf.FullName $dst -Force
  if (Test-Path (Join-Path $dst $lf.Name)) { Move-Item $lf.FullName "$done\" -Force; L "   OK  root file $($lf.Name)" }
}
L "DONE"

# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

| What | From | To now | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Code projects** | `C:\DEV\` | **`C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\`** | Sept 9–10 |
| **Documents** | `OneDrive - Baylor University\00_Primary_Storage_Drive` | **`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive`** | Sept 9–10 |

`C:\DEV` now holds only `_tools`, which contains the migration scripts and logs. That's why it looks empty. On Sept 10, `sync_from_github.ps1` moved the 16 projects that lived only in `C:\DEV` into `Desktop\DEV`. It then pulled 81 repos and cloned 50 more from GitHub (`erash11`). entries.description:
Call this tool to find general metadata about a user's Drive file.

Context window token management can be tuned via `snippetVerbosity` (default is `SnippetVerbosity.DETAILED`) or if only metadata is needed, use `excludeContentSnippets`.

If the file is not found, try using other tools like `search_files` to find the file the user is requesting.

excludeContentSnippets.description: If true, the content snippet will be excluded from the response.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to retrieve.

snippetVerbosity.description: Optional. Set to specify how verbose the snippets should be. Defaults to DETAILED if not set.
x-google-enum-descriptions: Limits the returned snippet to about 1000 characters.
Limits the returned snippet to about 2500 characters.
Limits the returned snippet to about 5000 characters.
The verbosity is greatly increased, limited by the overall response size.

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Google_Drive__search_files
entries.description:
Search for Drive files using a structured query (syntax: `query_term operator values`). Only terms in this list are supported.
Combine clauses with `and`, `or`, `not`, and parentheses. String values must be single-quoted; escape embedded quotes as `\'`.
Context window token management can be tuned via `snippetVerbosity` (default is `SnippetVerbosity.DETAILED`) or if only metadata is needed, use `excludeContentSnippets`.

Do NOT include document type terms (e.g., 'presentation', 'slides', 'deck', 'document', 'doc', 'spreadsheet', 'sheet', 'pdf', 'folder') inside `title contains '...'` or `fullText contains '...'` clauses. Separate title keywords from file type terms. Instead map them to `mimeType` clauses in the query (e.g., 'slides' -> `mimeType = 'application/vnd.google-apps.presentation'`).

Query terms & operators:

 - `title` (ops: contains, =, !=) — file title
 - `fullText` (ops: contains) — title or body text
 - `mimeType` (ops: contains, =, !=) — MIME type
 - `modifiedTime`, `viewedByMeTime`, `createdTime` (ops: `<=`, `<`, `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`). Use RFC 3339 UTC, e.g., `2012-06-04T12:00:00-08:00`. Date types not comparable.
 - `parentId` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Use `'root'` for the user's "My Drive".
 - `owner` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Use `'me'` for the requesting user.
 - `sharedWithMe` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Values: `true` or `false`.

Other operators: `and`, `or`, `not`.

Examples:

 - `title contains 'hello' and title contains 'goodbye'`
 - `modifiedTime > '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' and (mimeType contains 'image/' or mimeType contains 'video/')`
 - `parentId = '1234567'`
 - `fullText contains 'hello'`
 - `owner = 'test@example.org'`
 - `sharedWithMe = true`
 - `owner = 'me'` (for files owned by the user)

Use `next_page_token` to paginate. An empty response means no more results.

excludeContentSnippets.description: If true, the content snippet will be excluded from the response.

pageSize.description: The maximum number of files to return in each page.

pageToken.description: The page token to use for pagination.

snippetVerbosity.description: Optional. Set to specify how verbose the snippets should be. Defaults to DETAILED if not set.

Limits the returned snippet to about 2500 characters.

content.text:
**Yes to both, with one important limit on the Mac side.**

**Is `Desktop\DEV` backed up to Google Drive? Yes, and it's current.**
- Drive for Desktop on this laptop has exactly one backup folder registered: `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV`. It sits in the app's own settings, which I read directly.
- I confirmed from the cloud side that changes are arriving. Several `STATUS.md` files from DEV repos show up in Google Drive with timestamps from last night (latest 7:06 pm on 9/23).
- In Drive, the backup shows under **Computers → "My Laptop (2)" → DEV**. It isn't under My Drive, so you won't see it inside `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive`.

**Can the Mac get to those files? Yes, but only for reading. It's not a two-way sync.**
- **Where to find them:** on the web, drive.google.com → *Computers* → *My Laptop (2)* → *DEV*. On the Mac, Finder → Google Drive → *Other computers* → *My Laptop (2)* → *DEV*. I can only check from this laptop, so confirm that Finder path on the Mac.
- **The limit:** a "computer backup" only goes one way, from Windows up to Drive. If you edit a file there from the Mac, the change **does not** come back to the Windows `Desktop\DEV`, and you end up with two versions. Use it to grab a file, not to work in.
- **How the machines actually share work:**
  - **Code and docs inside a repo:** GitHub. Push on one machine, then `git pull` (or `dev-sync`) on the other into `~/DEV`.
  - **Documents:** `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive`. This one is a true two-way sync, visible and editable on both machines.
  - **Big data like the PFF DB:** Parquet snapshots in `pff-snapshots`. Never share the DB file itself.
- **Where the backup really helps:** files that git ignores (`.env`, local data extracts, Parquet in `data/`) never reach GitHub. Those exist only on this laptop plus the Drive backup, so that's the one place the Mac can get them.

Neither question needed any changes to your setup.

result: Yes: Drive for Desktop backs up `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV` to Drive as "My Laptop (2)" (changes through last night confirmed). The Mac can view those files under "Other computers", but edits there don't sync back, so keep using GitHub for code and `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` for shared documents.

I have what I need. Here's the verdict on sync only.

## Short answer: the design is right, with one real gap and one blind spot

**Working as intended (verified on Windows today):**

| What | How it moves | State |
|---|---|---|
| Code, repo docs, `STATUS.md` | GitHub, via `git pull` / `dev-sync` | `DEV`, `ContextVault` and the repos all even with GitHub |
| Claude setup: skills, hooks, settings, transcripts | GitHub (`dotclaude`, `claude-skills`) | Even; only today's in-flight transcripts are uncommitted, and the backup commits those |
| Global memory (`USER.md`, `MEMORY.md`, daily logs) | GitHub (`claude-global-memory`, `claude-memory-compiler`) | Even |
| SecondBrain | GitHub | Even, clean |
| Documents | `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive`, two-way | Live |
| PFF data | Parquet snapshots on Drive | Live |

Keep this split: git for anything text-like, Drive for documents, snapshot files for data. Don't collapse it into "sync the whole DEV folder through Drive." That path already cost you a locked DB and junction errors.

## Gap 1: project memory doesn't fully cross over

The memory files do sync, but each machine only auto-loads the folder named after its own path. For the DEV root:
- **43 memories written on the Mac never auto-load on Windows**
- 4 written on Windows never load on the Mac (`user_baylor-department-names`, `project_git-bash-msys-ad-stall`, `project_third-party-skill-install`, `project_backup-task-sleepkill-signature`)
- 3 more at the home-folder level are Windows-only

`memsearch` can still find the Mac ones (`memsearch-sync.js` indexes that folder), but only if a session thinks to search. Every other project's folders already match, because someone mirrored them once by hand. The DEV root has drifted since.

**Fix:** add a step to `dev-sync` (or the daily backup) that pairs each Mac folder with its Windows twin and copies missing files both ways, newest wins. It's about 30 lines. This is the one change that makes "all my context on both machines" true.

## Gap 2 (blind spot): files git ignores

`.env` files, local data extracts and Parquet outputs never reach GitHub.
- **Windows to Mac:** the Drive backup of `Desktop\DEV` covers this, read-only.
- **Mac to Windows:** I can't see from here whether the Mac's `~/DEV` is in a Drive backup. If it isn't, anything the Mac generates that git ignores exists only on the Mac.

Two rules close it:
- Anything the other machine needs to *use* goes in `00_Primary_Storage_Drive`, the way PFF does it.
- Secrets go in a password manager, never the backup.

Nothing was changed.

**Next step:** say the word and I'll build the memory mirror into `dev-sync` (worktree and PR). Separately, check on the Mac whether Drive for Desktop's backup folders include `~/DEV`.

result: The sync design (GitHub for code and Claude context, Drive for documents, Parquet for data) is sound and everything checked is current. The main gap: 43 Mac project memories never load on Windows (and 7 the other way), fixable with a small mirror step in `dev-sync`. Still unknown: whether the Mac's `~/DEV` is backed up to Drive.

1	---
2	name: dev-sync
3	description: >-
4	  Bring this machine into line with GitHub and load back the context that came with it:
5	  locate DEV automatically, pull config and skills, inventory every project, commit and
6	  push local work, pull the other machine's work, clone what is missing, report
7	  conflicts, then read the repo's STATUS and latest handoff and report where the last
8	  session left off. Use when Eric switches machines, sits down to start work, says 'sync
9	  DEV', asks whether everything is pushed, or asks where he left off. Do not use when
10	  Eric says '/startup' or 'good morning' (use startup, which runs this sync) or to
11	  scaffold a new repo (use new-project).
12	---
13	
14	# DEV sync
15	
16	Eric works on a Mac and a Windows laptop. GitHub (`erash11`, all private) is the transport. This skill makes the current machine match GitHub without losing anything on either side. It is the first thing to run when sitting down at a machine.
17	
18	## Step 0: find DEV (never depend on cwd)
19	
20	Eric may run this from anywhere. Detect the machine and go to its DEV root:
21	
22	- macOS (`uname` = Darwin): `~/DEV`
23	- Windows (PowerShell, or `$OS` = Windows_NT): `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV`
24	
25	If that folder does not exist, stop and say so. Do not guess another location. Print the root you chose on the first line of output.
26	
27	## Step 1: config and skills
28	
29	These are separate repos and the other machine may have changed them:
30	
31	1. `~/.claude` (repo `dotclaude`): `git pull`. If `~/.claude/machine.md` is missing, copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md` for this OS.
32	2. `~/.claude/skills` (repo `claude-skills`): `git pull`, then run `sync-to-codex.sh` (Mac) or `sync-to-codex.ps1` (Windows) so Codex sees the shared skills.
33	3. `~/.claude/global-memory` (repo `claude-global-memory`): `git pull`. **This is the only thing that carries memory between the two machines.** USER.md, MEMORY.md and the handoffs live here. `daily-backup` pushes this repo nightly, but nothing pulled it at the start of a session until this step existed, so a same-day handoff (worked on the Mac after lunch, picked up on Windows that evening) arrived with stale memory. Pull it before anything else reads it. If the pull brings in commits, say how many and name the newest, so it is visible that memory moved.
34	
35	If any of the three has local uncommitted changes, commit them first with `<machine> snapshot before sync`, then pull, then push.
36	
37	Merge note for `global-memory`: `transcripts/.errors.log` and `MEMORY.md` are both append-heavy and both machines write them. On conflict, keep both sides' content rather than choosing one — these are logs, not settings, and a dropped line is a lost memory.
38	
39	## Step 2: inventory (always show before changing anything)
40	
41	Walk `DEV/*`, `DEV/Football/*`, and `DEV/SpecialRequests/*`. Skip `.claude`, `_tools`, `_DRIVE` (a link to the Google Drive primary storage drive, not a project; never init it, never walk into it), `token-dashboard` (someone else's remote), and any folder ending in `_OLD_merged*`. For each folder report one of:
42	
43	- **repo + erash11 remote**: uncommitted count, unpushed count
44	- **repo, no remote**: needs `gh repo create`
45	- **not a repo**: needs init + create (use the `new-project` skill's file set)
46	
47	Then `gh repo list erash11 --limit 300 --json name` and list repos with no local folder. Skip: `dotclaude` (that is `~/.claude`), `SecondBrain`, `claude-skills`, `claude-memory-compiler`, `DEV`, `DexaProject`.
48	
49	Eric pre-approves these operations; the inventory is for visibility, not a pause for approval, unless something looks wrong (a repo with hundreds of uncommitted files, a large file about to be added).
50	
51	**Group the report by activity, not alphabetically.** Run `~/.claude/scripts/dev-activity.sh` (Mac) or `dev-activity.ps1` (Windows), which ranks repos by distinct commit days over 90 days. List the active ones individually and collapse the rest to a count: "118 dormant repos: all clean" is the useful line, not 118 names. About 14 repos are genuinely worked at any time; the rest are archives that happen to live in the same folder.
52	
53	Rank by **commit days, not recency**. On 2026-09-09 a bulk migration gave 43 repos one commit each, after which every one of them looked active by any recency measure. Days-worked is not fooled by that, because a migration touches a repo once.
54	
55	Nothing is archived or moved on the strength of this. Sorting is a reporting concern. Moving a dormant repo into an archive folder would break three things at once: `harvest-dev-docs` reads `<dir>/docs/*.md` without recursing, so archived repos would silently drop out of the memsearch index; KeystoneOS `projects.json`, `memory-sources.json`, `memory-index-paths.json` and `discovery-roots.json` hold DEV paths; and Tier A project memory is keyed by a slug derived from the absolute path, so moving a repo orphans its memory. Checked 2026-09-12. Do not revive the archive idea without fixing all three first.
56	
57	## Step 3: apply, per repo
58	
59	1. If uncommitted: put any untracked file over 95 MB and any `.env` into `.gitignore`, then `git add -A && git commit -m "<machine> snapshot before sync"`.
60	2. `git fetch origin` then `git merge --no-edit origin/<branch>`.
61	3. On conflict: keep this machine's version, save the remote version beside it as `<file>.from-mac` or `<file>.from-windows` (whichever the other machine is), stage both, commit. Never discard either side. `.DS_Store` conflicts: just delete the file.
62	
63	   Save the remote side by **moving the file, never by redirecting stdout**. A
64	   redirect re-encodes the bytes; on Windows that silently mangles every
65	   non-ASCII character (an em-dash becomes `ΓÇö`) and adds a UTF-8 BOM, so the
66	   saved copy is corrupt and every later diff shows a phantom first-line change.
67	
68	   - PowerShell: `git checkout --theirs -- <f>; Move-Item <f> <f>.from-mac; git checkout --ours -- <f>`
69	   - bash: `git checkout --theirs -- <f> && mv <f> <f>.from-mac && git checkout --ours -- <f>`
70	
71	   Never run `git add -A` while `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists — it stages the
72	   conflict markers themselves and commits a broken file. Stage only the named
73	   paths you just resolved.
74	4. `git push`.
75	5. Missing locally: `gh repo clone erash11/<name> DEV/<name>`.
76	6. No remote: `gh repo create erash11/<name> --private --source=. --push`.
77	
78	Windows note: line-ending noise (`LF will be replaced by CRLF`) is normal. If a merge refuses to start because of phantom modifications, run `git add --renormalize .` and commit before merging.
79	
80	Stale-lock note: if a commit or push fails with `cannot lock ref 'HEAD'`, check
81	`pgrep -fl git` (or `Get-Process git`) first. If no git is running and the
82	`.git/*.lock` file is zero bytes and older than the session, it is stale from an
83	interrupted run. Move it aside — do not delete it — then retry.
84	
85	## Step 4: verify and report
86	
87	Re-walk every repo. Report: DEV root used, config and skills pulled (yes/no), repos checked, pulled, cloned, created, and any folder still dirty or unpushed. List every `.from-*` file created so Eric can reconcile them. Finish with one line: clean or not.
88	
89	## Step 5: pick up where the other machine left off
90	
91	Syncing git state is only half the job. The other half is loading the context that came with it, and nothing else does this — the SessionStart hook injects global memory, but project state lives in the repo, and Tier A project memory does not cross machines because its slug is built from a path that differs per machine. This step is the only place that context gets read back in.
92	
93	Do this for the repo Eric names, or the one he is in. If he has not named one, pick from the ACTIVE list in Step 2, not from all 132: take the active repo with the most recent commit and say which you chose. A dormant repo receiving one migration commit must never win this, which is exactly what picking by recency across everything would do.
94	
95	1. Read `<repo>/AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md` if there is no AGENTS.md).
96	2. Read `<repo>/docs/STATUS.md`.
97	3. Read the newest file in `<repo>/docs/handoffs/`, if the folder exists and its newest file is within about two weeks.
98	4. If `docs/STATUS.md` does not exist in a repo that has real work in it, say so — that repo is invisible to the other machine and closeout should have created it.
99	
100	Then report, in six lines or fewer, before doing any work:
101	
102	```
103	Picking up: <repo>
104	Last session: <date>, <mac|windows>
105	Where things stand: <two lines from STATUS.md Current state>
106	Blocked on: <open questions, or "nothing">
107	Next: <top one or two from STATUS.md Next>
108	```
109	
110	Stop there and wait for Eric to confirm or redirect. Do not start the next task off the back of STATUS.md on your own — it records where work stopped, not what he wants to do this morning.
111	
112	## Do not
113	
114	- Do not `rm` anything. Move to a `_to_delete` or `_OLD_*` folder if something must get out of the way.
115	- Do not rebase or force-push.
116	- Do not push DexaProject or any repo whose CLAUDE.md says its data must stay local.

2. `~/.claude/skills` (repo `claude-skills`): `git pull`, then run `sync-to-codex.sh` (Mac) or `sync-to-codex.ps1` (Windows) so Codex sees the shared skills.
3. `~/.claude/global-memory` (repo `claude-global-memory`): `git pull`. **This is the only thing that carries memory between the two machines.** USER.md, MEMORY.md and the handoffs live here. `daily-backup` pushes this repo nightly, but nothing pulled it at the start of a session until this step existed, so a same-day handoff (worked on the Mac after lunch, picked up on Windows that evening) arrived with stale memory. Pull it before anything else reads it. If the pull brings in commits, say how many and name the newest, so it is visible that memory moved.

If any of the three has local uncommitted changes, commit them first with `<machine> snapshot before sync`, then pull, then push.

Merge note for `global-memory`: `transcripts/.errors.log` and `MEMORY.md` are both append-heavy and both machines write them. On conflict, keep both sides' content rather than choosing one — these are logs, not settings, and a dropped line is a lost memory.

## Step 2: inventory (always show before changing anything)

Walk `DEV/*`, `DEV/Football/*`, and `DEV/SpecialRequests/*`. Skip `.claude`, `_tools`, `_DRIVE` (a link to the Google Drive primary storage drive, not a project; never init it, never walk into it), `token-dashboard` (someone else's remote), and any folder ending in `_OLD_merged*`. For each folder report one of:

- **repo + erash11 remote**: uncommitted count, unpushed count
- **repo, no remote**: needs `gh repo create`
- **not a repo**: needs init + create (use the `new-project` skill's file set)

Then `gh repo list erash11 --limit 300 --json name` and list repos with no local folder. Skip: `dotclaude` (that is `~/.claude`), `SecondBrain`, `claude-skills`, `claude-memory-compiler`, `DEV`, `DexaProject`.

Eric pre-approves these operations; the inventory is for visibility, not a pause for approval, unless something looks wrong (a repo with hundreds of uncommitted files, a large file about to be added).

**Group the report by activity, not alphabetically.** Run `~/.claude/scripts/dev-activity.sh` (Mac) or `dev-activity.ps1` (Windows), which ranks repos by distinct commit days over 90 days. List the active ones individually and collapse the rest to a count: "118 dormant repos: all clean" is the useful line, not 118 names. About 14 repos are genuinely worked at any time; the rest are archives that happen to live in the same folder.

Rank by **commit days, not recency**. On 2026-09-09 a bulk migration gave 43 repos one commit each, after which every one of them looked active by any recency measure. Days-worked is not fooled by that, because a migration touches a repo once.

Nothing is archived or moved on the strength of this. Sorting is a reporting concern. Moving a dormant repo into an archive folder would break three things at once: `harvest-dev-docs` reads `<dir>/docs/*.md` without recursing, so archived repos would silently drop out of the memsearch index; KeystoneOS `projects.json`, `memory-sources.json`, `memory-index-paths.json` and `discovery-roots.json` hold DEV paths; and Tier A project memory is keyed by a slug derived from the absolute path, so moving a repo orphans its memory. Checked 2026-09-12. Do not revive the archive idea without fixing all three first.

## Step 3: apply, per repo

1. If uncommitted: put any untracked file over 95 MB and any `.env` into `.gitignore`, then `git add -A && git commit -m "<machine> snapshot before sync"`.
2. `git fetch origin` then `git merge --no-edit origin/<branch>`.
3. On conflict: keep this machine's version, save the remote version beside it as `<file>.from-mac` or `<file>.from-windows` (whichever the other machine is), stage both, commit. Never discard either side. `.DS_Store` conflicts: just delete the file.

   Save the remote side by **moving the file, never by redirecting stdout**. A
   redirect re-encodes the bytes; on Windows that silently mangles every
   non-ASCII character (an em-dash becomes `ΓÇö`) and adds a UTF-8 BOM, so the
   saved copy is corrupt and every later diff shows a phantom first-line change.

   - PowerShell: `git checkout --theirs -- <f>; Move-Item <f> <f>.from-mac; git checkout --ours -- <f>`
   - bash: `git checkout --theirs -- <f> && mv <f> <f>.from-mac && git checkout --ours -- <f>`

   Never run `git add -A` while `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists — it stages the
   conflict markers themselves and commits a broken file. Stage only the named
   paths you just resolved.
4. `git push`.
5. Missing locally: `gh repo clone erash11/<name> DEV/<name>`.
6. No remote: `gh repo create erash11/<name> --private --source=. --push`.

Windows note: line-ending noise (`LF will be replaced by CRLF`) is normal. If a merge refuses to start because of phantom modifications, run `git add --renormalize .` and commit before merging.

Stale-lock note: if a commit or push fails with `cannot lock ref 'HEAD'`, check
`pgrep -fl git` (or `Get-Process git`) first. If no git is running and the
`.git/*.lock` file is zero bytes and older than the session, it is stale from an
interrupted run. Move it aside — do not delete it — then retry.

## Step 4: verify and report

Re-walk every repo. Report: DEV root used, config and skills pulled (yes/no), repos checked, pulled, cloned, created, and any folder still dirty or unpushed. List every `.from-*` file created so Eric can reconcile them. Finish with one line: clean or not.

## Step 5: pick up where the other machine left off

Syncing git state is only half the job. The other half is loading the context that came with it, and nothing else does this — the SessionStart hook injects global memory, but project state lives in the repo, and Tier A project memory does not cross machines because its slug is built from a path that differs per machine. This step is the only place that context gets read back in.

Do this for the repo Eric names, or the one he is in. If he has not named one, pick from the ACTIVE list in Step 2, not from all 132: take the active repo with the most recent commit and say which you chose. A dormant repo receiving one migration commit must never win this, which is exactly what picking by recency across everything would do.

1. Read `<repo>/AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md` if there is no AGENTS.md).
2. Read `<repo>/docs/STATUS.md`.
3. Read the newest file in `<repo>/docs/handoffs/`, if the folder exists and its newest file is within about two weeks.
4. If `docs/STATUS.md` does not exist in a repo that has real work in it, say so — that repo is invisible to the other machine and closeout should have created it.

Then report, in six lines or fewer, before doing any work:

```
Picking up: <repo>
Last session: <date>, <mac|windows>
Where things stand: <two lines from STATUS.md Current state>
Blocked on: <open questions, or "nothing">
Next: <top one or two from STATUS.md Next>
```

Stop there and wait for Eric to confirm or redirect. Do not start the next task off the back of STATUS.md on your own — it records where work stopped, not what he wants to do this morning.

## Do not

- Do not `rm` anything. Move to a `_to_delete` or `_OLD_*` folder if something must get out of the way.
- Do not rebase or force-push.
- Do not push DexaProject or any repo whose CLAUDE.md says its data must stay local.

---
name: dev-sync
description: >-
  Bring this machine into line with GitHub and load back the context that came with it:
  locate DEV automatically, pull config and skills, inventory every project, commit and
  push local work, pull the other machine's work, clone what is missing, report
  conflicts, then read the repo's STATUS and latest handoff and report where the last
  session left off. Use when Eric switches machines, sits down to start work, says 'sync
  DEV', asks whether everything is pushed, or asks where he left off. Do not use when
  Eric says '/startup' or 'good morning' (use startup, which runs this sync) or to
  scaffold a new repo (use new-project).
---

# DEV sync

Eric works on a Mac and a Windows laptop. GitHub (`erash11`, all private) is the transport. This skill makes the current machine match GitHub without losing anything on either side. It is the first thing to run when sitting down at a machine.

## Step 0: find DEV (never depend on cwd)

Eric may run this from anywhere. Detect the machine and go to its DEV root:

- macOS (`uname` = Darwin): `~/DEV`
- Windows (PowerShell, or `$OS` = Windows_NT): `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV`

If that folder does not exist, stop and say so. Do not guess another location. Print the root you chose on the first line of output.

## Step 1: config and skills

These are separate repos and the other machine may have changed them:

1. `~/.claude` (repo `dotclaude`): `git pull`. If `~/.claude/machine.md` is missing, copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md` for this OS.
2. `~/.claude/skills` (repo `claude-skills`): `git pull`, then run `sync-to-codex.sh` (Mac) or `sync-to-codex.ps1` (Windows) so Codex sees the shared skills.
3. `~/.claude/global-memory` (repo `claude-global-memory`): `git pull`. **This is the only thing that carries memory between the two machines.** USER.md, MEMORY.md and the handoffs live here. `daily-backup` pushes this repo nightly, but nothing pulled it at the start of a session until this step existed, so a same-day handoff (worked on the Mac after lunch, picked up on Windows that evening) arrived with stale memory. Pull it before anything else reads it. If the pull brings in commits, say how many and name the newest, so it is visible that memory moved.

If any of the three has local uncommitted changes, commit them first with `<machine> snapshot before sync`, then pull, then push.

Merge note for `global-memory`: `transcripts/.errors.log` and `MEMORY.md` are both append-heavy and both machines write them. On conflict, keep both sides' content rather than choosing one — these are logs, not settings, and a dropped line is a lost memory.

## Step 2: inventory (always show before changing anything)

Walk `DEV/*`, `DEV/Football/*`, and `DEV/SpecialRequests/*`. Skip `.claude`, `_tools`, `_DRIVE` (a link to the Google Drive primary storage drive, not a project; never init it, never walk into it), `token-dashboard` (someone else's remote), and any folder ending in `_OLD_merged*`. For each folder report one of:

- **repo + erash11 remote**: uncommitted count, unpushed count
- **repo, no remote**: needs `gh repo create`
- **not a repo**: needs init + create (use the `new-project` skill's file set)

Then `gh repo list erash11 --limit 300 --json name` and list repos with no local folder. Skip: `dotclaude` (that is `~/.claude`), `SecondBrain`, `claude-skills`, `claude-memory-compiler`, `DEV`, `DexaProject`.

Eric pre-approves these operations; the inventory is for visibility, not a pause for approval, unless something looks wrong (a repo with hundreds of uncommitted files, a large file about to be added).

**Group the report by activity, not alphabetically.** Run `~/.claude/scripts/dev-activity.sh` (Mac) or `dev-activity.ps1` (Windows), which ranks repos by distinct commit days over 90 days. List the active ones individually and collapse the rest to a count: "118 dormant repos: all clean" is the useful line, not 118 names. About 14 repos are genuinely worked at any time; the rest are archives that happen to live in the same folder.

Rank by **commit days, not recency**. On 2026-09-09 a bulk migration gave 43 repos one commit each, after which every one of them looked active by any recency measure. Days-worked is not fooled by that, because a migration touches a repo once.

Nothing is archived or moved on the strength of this. Sorting is a reporting concern. Moving a dormant repo into an archive folder would break three things at once: `harvest-dev-docs` reads `<dir>/docs/*.md` without recursing, so archived repos would silently drop out of the memsearch index; KeystoneOS `projects.json`, `memory-sources.json`, `memory-index-paths.json` and `discovery-roots.json` hold DEV paths; and Tier A project memory is keyed by a slug derived from the absolute path, so moving a repo orphans its memory. Checked 2026-09-12. Do not revive the archive idea without fixing all three first.

## Step 3: apply, per repo

1. If uncommitted: put any untracked file over 95 MB and any `.env` into `.gitignore`, then `git add -A && git commit -m "<machine> snapshot before sync"`.
2. `git fetch origin` then `git merge --no-edit origin/<branch>`.
3. On conflict: keep this machine's version, save the remote version beside it as `<file>.from-mac` or `<file>.from-windows` (whichever the other machine is), stage both, commit. Never discard either side. `.DS_Store` conflicts: just delete the file.

   Save the remote side by **moving the file, never by redirecting stdout**. A

# Handoff — 2026-09-21 — The Mac owns the GPS, Perch and VALD pulls

## What and why

The session started with a Mac `/dev-sync`. Eric then made the Mac the one machine that pulls the three
athlete data feeds: Catapult GPS, Perch (1RM) and VALD ForceDecks (CMJ + IMTP). Before this, Perch was
decided as Windows-owned (09-20), VALD had no working pull anywhere since 2026-08-02, and GPS ran on the
Mac at 06:30 and failed when the Mac slept.

## Decisions (with the reasoning)

- **All three pulls live on the Mac.** Eric briefly chose Windows for GPS, then reversed the same
  afternoon. One writer per database: two gitignored caches drift apart without any conflict warning.
- **Pull times moved to business hours:** GPS 10:00 + 16:30, Perch 10:05 + 16:35, VALD 10:10 + 16:40.
  The Mac is awake then, so the `pmset` wake question is dropped. The jobs are 5 minutes apart so they
  do not overlap.
- **Perch was refilled from the API, not copied from Windows.** `perch_ingest.py` upserts by
  athlete/exercise/date, and each run re-derives from the API, so the Windows copy was not needed.
  Result: 13,436 rows through 2026-09-21, more than the Windows copy (13,346 on 09-19).
- **Scheduled runs pull a short window:** Perch = the last 14 days from the newest stored test_date. VALD =
  from 3 days before the last successful run (the VALD API filters by `modifiedFromUtc`).
- **Token and secret rotation skipped for now** (Catapult token, VALD client secret). Eric's call; the
  repos are private and the pulls work.

## Root cause of the VALD failure

`src/ingest/pipeline.py` had `client: "VALDClient" | None`. Python evaluates that at import time and
raises TypeError before 3.14, so every entry point crashed on import. Fixed by quoting the whole hint.
Separately, the Windows `.bat` called `pipeline.py`, which has no entry point; the real one is
`run_pipeline.py`.

## Files created or modified

- `~/DEV/DataBase_GPS_Reporting/ops/com.keystone.gpspull.plist` (times), `gps_report/pull.sh` (comment),
  `docs/STATUS.md`
- `~/DEV/PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026/pull_perch.sh` (new), `ops/com.keystone.perchpull.plist` (new),
  `.gitignore`, `docs/STATUS.md`; `.venv/` (new, uv); `data/backups/perch_pre-backfill_2026-09-21.duckdb`
- `~/DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/src/ingest/pipeline.py` (fix), `pull_vald.sh` (new),
  `ops/com.keystone.valdpull.plist` (new), `.gitignore`, `docs/STATUS.md`; `.venv/` (new, uv);
  `data/backups/forceplate_pre-mac-pull_2026-09-21.db`
- `~/DEV/_INBOX/refresh_all_data.bat` (step 1 REM'd; step 3 was REM'd by the Windows session in PR #3,
  merged), `docs/STATUS.md`
- `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.{gpspull,perchpull,valdpull}.plist` (installed and loaded)
- `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (GPS and VALD+Perch lines),
  `transcripts/2026-09-19.md` and `2026-09-21.md` (merge conflicts resolved by keeping both sides)
- Drive: `02_SPORTS/Football/FA2026/_Mark_for_Deletion/gps_db_handoff_2026-09-21/` (the unused GPS DB
  copy, safe to delete)

## First scheduled afternoon runs (2026-09-21) — all passed, two ran late

- GPS 16:32: ok, exit 0, no new sessions (DB newest 2026-09-19).
- Perch and VALD: the Mac idle-slept at 15:45, so both started at 16:45:33 on a wake and then crept
  through DarkWakes (brief background wakes with no usable network). VALD finished ok at 17:36. Perch
  hit two read timeouts and passed on attempt 3 at 17:39 (DB newest 2026-09-21). No alerts fired.
- Open for Eric: `sudo pmset repeat wakeorpoweron MTWRFSU 16:28:00` to wake the Mac for the afternoon
  runs (recommended), or leave it and accept late runs. Morning runs at 10:00 usually find it awake.

## Next actions

Both checks are done. Windows does have the credentials: a Fireflies key in its environment and a `gws` login (your 5 pm Gmail digest uses it). So meetings and email aren't stuck on the Mac. The GPS status page doesn't say where the Power BI report gets its data, so I'll flag that as unknown rather than guess.

## Verdict: yes, work on Windows by day and the Mac at night, with three conditions

Almost all of your *working* context already reaches both machines: code, skills, memory (after this morning's mirror), documents and PFF data. What stays on the Mac is its scheduled jobs and the data they produce. The split works if you handle those.

1. **The Mac stays on and awake at home during the day.** It runs the GPS, Perch and VALD pulls at 10:00 and 16:30. On 9/21 it fell asleep at 3:45 pm and the afternoon pulls finished an hour late. You chose not to schedule a wake, which made sense while you worked on the Mac. It stops making sense once you don't. Run this once on the Mac: `sudo pmset repeat wakeorpoweron MTWRFSU 09:58:00` (plus a second wake at 16:28, since `pmset repeat` holds only one; plugged in with "prevent sleep" does the same job).
2. **The pulled data has to reach Windows.** `gps_history.duckdb`, `perch.duckdb` and `forceplate.db` exist **only on the Mac**, while Power BI and VALD ForceDecks exist **only on Windows**. Copy what PFF already does: after each pull, write Parquet snapshots to Drive and have Windows read those. Keep the Mac as the only writer. This is the one real build item. First find out where `03_REPORTS\2026_GPS_Report.pbix` gets its data. If it points at an old Windows copy of the GPS database, that copy has been stale since 9/21.
3. **Windows pushes at the end of the day.** The nightly auto-push script (`daily-backup`) refuses to run on Windows, so nothing pushes Windows' memory or config for you. Run closeout (or `dev-sync`) before switching to the Mac. Otherwise the Mac starts the evening with stale memory.

## Inventory

**Runs only on the Mac** (reconstructed from synced files; confirm tonight with `launchctl list | grep keystone`):

| Job | When | Notes for the split |
|---|---|---|
| GPS / Perch / VALD pulls | 10:00 and 16:30, weekdays | Needs the Mac awake; data needs an export (conditions 1 and 2) |
| daily-backup (pushes repos, copies to Drive and the CRASHBOX SSD) | 09:00 | Consider moving to the evening, when you're actually on the Mac |
| reconcile (reruns missed jobs) | 07:00 and at login | Fine |
| ritual nudges (interview-me, weekly-review, …) | 17:00 weekdays, Fri 15:30 | They fire as pop-ups on the Mac while you're on Windows, so you'll miss them. Move to Windows (the original version used `msg.exe`) or to evening |
| CommandCentre status page, localhost:7373 | always on | Not reachable from Windows. Only matters if you use it by day |
| KeystoneOS morning, agy sync, weekly memory review (adjudicate), graph extraction, monthly metrics (aiosaudit) | various | Background work, fine unattended |
| CFB forecast capture | manual, Mac-only by decision (9/23) | Evening work anyway |

**Other Mac-only items:** the CRASHBOX SSD backup, Keychain secrets, the `S2_Evaluation\data` folder, and scripts written for macOS (graph-extraction loop, `skill-button.sh`).

**Runs only on Windows:** Power BI Desktop, VALD ForceDecks Suite, Docker + Milvus for memsearch (the Mac removed Docker 9/3), Drive backup of `Desktop\DEV`, the Gmail digest (5 pm), and the AI-session backup to Drive. **That backup failed this morning (exit code 1). Run `/claude-stack-doctor` to fix it.**

**On both:** the stack doctor, the custom CLIs (ESPN, Fireflies, Zotero, Catapult), `gws`, Fireflies, Zotero, Obsidian, SecondBrain, RStudio, Codex and Claude Code.

**Resolved along the way:** the GPS status page still lists the Windows GPS writer as "not verified stopped". It is stopped: `Refresh_All_Data` is disabled, last ran 9/20. Its old KeystoneOS copies are all disabled too, so nothing runs twice.

**The daily routine:** morning on Windows, run `dev-sync`. End of day, run closeout. Evening on the Mac, run `dev-sync`. At night, the Mac pushes by itself.

I can save this ownership table to a repo's `docs/` so both machines can see it, and build the Parquet export for the three pulls (condition 2). Neither is started.

Everything else is already on both machines, apart from the Mac's scheduled jobs and a few Mac-only items listed above.

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

input.prompt:
You are building a feature across three git repos on Eric's Windows laptop. Work carefully; this is athlete data.

## Context
Eric uses a Mac (evenings) and this Windows laptop (daytime primary). The Mac is the ONLY writer of three athlete-data databases, pulled by launchd on the Mac at 10:00 and 16:30 weekdays:
- Catapult GPS -> `gps_history.duckdb` — repo `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\DataBase_GPS_Reporting` (pull script `gps_report/pull.sh`, plist `ops/com.keystone.gpspull.plist`)
- Perch 1RM -> `perch.duckdb` — repo `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026` (`pull_perch.sh`, `ops/com.keystone.perchpull.plist`, `perch_ingest.py`)
- VALD ForceDecks -> `forceplate.db` — repo `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` (`pull_vald.sh`, `run_pipeline.py`, `src/ingest/pipeline.py`)
Background: `C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\global-memory\handoffs\2026-09-21-mac-owns-data-pulls.md`. Rule: one writer per database; Windows must never write these DBs.
Goal: Windows needs daytime READ access to this data. The proven pattern is in `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\Football\PFF_Data_Project` — read `scripts/export_snapshot.py`, `src/` snapshot code, `tests/test_snapshot.py`, and its CLAUDE.md "Moving data between machines" section, and mirror its style (Drive root resolution, manifest.json, machine name, idempotence).

## Spec
In EACH of the three repos add an export step that, after a successful pull, writes Parquet snapshots of the DB's tables to Google Drive:
- Root: env var `ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR` if set, else the OS default `.../00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots` (Mac: `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots`; Windows: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\athlete-snapshots`). Subfolder per source: `gps/`, `perch/`, `vald/`. One `<table>.parquet` per table (skip internal/log tables only if clearly operational; state which) plus `manifest.json` in the source folder recording per table: rows, bytes, written_at (UTC ISO), machine (hostname), source DB newest date if a date column is obvious.
- Atomic writes: write `<table>.parquet.tmp` then replace, so Drive never syncs a half file.
- Stale-writer guard: refuse to overwrite a table whose existing manifest row count is GREATER than the new export's (data only grows via upserts) unless `--force`; print a clear message. This protects against a stale Windows copy clobbering the Mac's snapshot.
- Use duckdb (`COPY ... TO ... (FORMAT PARQUET)`) for .duckdb; for `forceplate.db` first determine whether it is SQLite or DuckDB and handle accordingly (duckdb can read sqlite via its sqlite extension, or use sqlite3+pandas/pyarrow — pick whatever the repo already depends on; do not add heavy deps).
- Hook it into the pull shell script after a successful pull. An export failure must be logged loudly but must NOT change the pull's exit status (the pull succeeded). Put the export result into the existing `logs/last_run.json` receipt if there is a natural place.
- Never print athlete names or row contents — counts and table names only (VALD stdout already leaks names in FLAG: lines; don't add more).
- Tests (pytest) using temp DBs and a temp snapshot dir, covering: export writes files + manifest, atomic replace, stale-writer guard refuses and --force overrides. No live API, no real Drive, no real DBs.
- Update each repo's docs/STATUS.md (and README/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md where the data-flow is documented — respect any CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md mirroring rule or pre-commit hook in that repo) with: where the snapshots land, that Windows reads Parquet directly (e.g. `duckdb.sql("select * from 'G:/My Drive/.../athlete-snapshots/gps/<table>.parquet'")`), and that only the Mac writes.

## Rules
- Read each repo's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md first and follow it.
- Do NOT edit the shared checkouts. For each repo: `git -C <repo> fetch origin` then `git -C <repo> worktree add C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\jobs\35a8d3c2\tmp\wt-<short> -b parquet-export origin/<default branch>` and work there. Run tests there (use the repo's existing venv/uv setup if present, else `uv run --with` or a temp venv — don't modify global Python).
- Do NOT write to the real Drive snapshot folder and do NOT open the real DB files for writing. You may read a real local DB copy read-only only to learn table names/schemas; don't print contents.
- Commit (end message with the two lines below), push the branch, open a PR with `gh pr create` (body ends with the line `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`). Never push to main, never force-push, don't merge.
  Commit trailer:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YMb1eLQB5TGh1zQAX34PUL
- After pushing, remove each worktree with `git worktree remove`.
- If something in the spec conflicts with what the repo actually does, adapt sensibly and report it.

Return: per repo — PR URL, tables exported, test results (pass counts), the exact command Eric runs on the Mac to do a first manual export, and anything you could not verify.
