1	# Ritual guard.
2	#
3	# The 2026-07-24 audits found one pattern in all three systems: everything with
4	# a cron stayed alive, everything manual froze. interview-me and weekly-review
5	# both died on 2026-06-05 and nothing noticed for 49 days, because a missing
6	# ritual leaves no error — it leaves an absence, and absences are invisible.
7	#
8	# A cron cannot conduct an interview. What it CAN do is notice the gap and put
9	# it somewhere unavoidable. That is all this does.
10	#
11	# Usage:
12	#   .\scripts\ritual-check.ps1            # report (runs in the morning cadence)
13	#   .\scripts\ritual-check.ps1 -Notify    # also raise a desktop prompt if due
14	#   .\scripts\ritual-check.ps1 -Json      # machine-readable, for the dashboard
15	
16	[CmdletBinding()]
17	param(
18	    [switch]$Notify,
19	    [switch]$Json,
20	    # Overridable so tests can point at a fixture vault. $Root already follows
21	    # $PSScriptRoot, so copying this script into a temp root redirects the
22	    # decisions-log lookup for free; only the vault needed a seam.
23	    [string]$Vault = "/Users/kristinarash/SecondBrain",
24	    # Same seam rationale as $Vault: the CFB snapshots live outside both $Root and
25	    # $Vault, so tests need their own pointer at a fixture directory.
26	    [string]$CfbSnapshotDir = "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots",
27	    # forecast-capture's status depends on the day of the week and on a season
28	    # window, so it cannot be tested without pinning "now". Defaults to the real
29	    # clock; only tests pass this.
30	    [datetime]$Today = (Get-Date),
31	    # The slate rules live in project-triage (slate.py, tested there). Absolute
32	    # interpreter path because launchd runs with a bare PATH.
33	    [string]$Python = "/opt/homebrew/bin/python3",
34	    [string]$PortfolioScript = "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py",
35	    # Empty = the live registry next to portfolio.py. Tests pass a fixture.
36	    [string]$SlateRegistry = ""
37	)
38	
39	$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
40	$Root  = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
41	$today = $Today
42	
43	# Read the ritual's own output as the record of when it last ran. Deliberately
44	# not a separate state file: a state file can drift from reality, the artifact
45	# cannot. If the note exists, the ritual ran.
46	function Get-LastRun {
47	    param([string]$Path, [string]$Filter)
48	    $f = Get-ChildItem $Path -File -Filter $Filter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
49	         Sort-Object Name -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
50	    if (-not $f) { return $null }
51	    # Prefer the date in the filename over mtime — cloud sync and bulk git ops
52	    # touch mtimes wholesale and would silently reset the clock.
53	    if ($f.Name -match '^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})') {
54	        return [pscustomobject]@{ Date = Get-Date "$($Matches[1])-$($Matches[2])-$($Matches[3])"; File = $f.Name }
55	    }
56	    return [pscustomobject]@{ Date = $f.LastWriteTime.Date; File = $f.Name }
57	}
58	
59	$rituals = @()
60	
61	# --- interview-me: end-of-workday distillation into permanent notes ----------
62	$iv = Get-LastRun -Path "$Vault\Inbox" -Filter "*interview*.md"
63	$ivDays = if ($iv) { [int]($today.Date - $iv.Date).TotalDays } else { 9999 }
64	$rituals += [pscustomobject]@{
65	    Name    = "interview-me"
66	    Command = "/interview-me"
67	    Last    = if ($iv) { $iv.Date.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { "never" }
68	    Days    = $ivDays
69	    # Weekday ritual. Due after 2 days, overdue after 5 (a full working week missed).
70	    Status  = if ($ivDays -ge 5) { "OVERDUE" } elseif ($ivDays -ge 2) { "DUE" } else { "OK" }
71	    Why     = "distils the workday into atomic permanent notes; SecondBrain\Notes\ is fed by nothing else"
72	}
73	
74	# --- weekly-review: Friday close-of-week synthesis ---------------------------
75	$wr = Get-LastRun -Path "$Vault\Inbox\weekly-review" -Filter "*.md"
76	$wrDays = if ($wr) { [int]($today.Date - $wr.Date).TotalDays } else { 9999 }

# Ritual guard.
#
# The 2026-07-24 audits found one pattern in all three systems: everything with
# a cron stayed alive, everything manual froze. interview-me and weekly-review
# both died on 2026-06-05 and nothing noticed for 49 days, because a missing
# ritual leaves no error — it leaves an absence, and absences are invisible.
#
# A cron cannot conduct an interview. What it CAN do is notice the gap and put
# it somewhere unavoidable. That is all this does.
#
# Usage:
#   .\scripts\ritual-check.ps1            # report (runs in the morning cadence)
#   .\scripts\ritual-check.ps1 -Notify    # also raise a desktop prompt if due
#   .\scripts\ritual-check.ps1 -Json      # machine-readable, for the dashboard

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$Notify,
    [switch]$Json,
    # Overridable so tests can point at a fixture vault. $Root already follows
    # $PSScriptRoot, so copying this script into a temp root redirects the
    # decisions-log lookup for free; only the vault needed a seam.
    [string]$Vault = "/Users/kristinarash/SecondBrain",
    # Same seam rationale as $Vault: the CFB snapshots live outside both $Root and
    # $Vault, so tests need their own pointer at a fixture directory.
    [string]$CfbSnapshotDir = "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots",
    # forecast-capture's status depends on the day of the week and on a season
    # window, so it cannot be tested without pinning "now". Defaults to the real
    # clock; only tests pass this.
    [datetime]$Today = (Get-Date),
    # The slate rules live in project-triage (slate.py, tested there). Absolute
    # interpreter path because launchd runs with a bare PATH.
    [string]$Python = "/opt/homebrew/bin/python3",
    [string]$PortfolioScript = "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py",
    # Empty = the live registry next to portfolio.py. Tests pass a fixture.
    [string]$SlateRegistry = ""
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$Root  = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$today = $Today

# Read the ritual's own output as the record of when it last ran. Deliberately
# not a separate state file: a state file can drift from reality, the artifact
# cannot. If the note exists, the ritual ran.
function Get-LastRun {
    param([string]$Path, [string]$Filter)
    $f = Get-ChildItem $Path -File -Filter $Filter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
         Sort-Object Name -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $f) { return $null }
    # Prefer the date in the filename over mtime — cloud sync and bulk git ops
    # touch mtimes wholesale and would silently reset the clock.
    if ($f.Name -match '^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})') {
        return [pscustomobject]@{ Date = Get-Date "$($Matches[1])-$($Matches[2])-$($Matches[3])"; File = $f.Name }
    }
    return [pscustomobject]@{ Date = $f.LastWriteTime.Date; File = $f.Name }
}

$rituals = @()

# --- interview-me: end-of-workday distillation into permanent notes ----------
$iv = Get-LastRun -Path "$Vault\Inbox" -Filter "*interview*.md"
$ivDays = if ($iv) { [int]($today.Date - $iv.Date).TotalDays } else { 9999 }
$rituals += [pscustomobject]@{
    Name    = "interview-me"
    Command = "/interview-me"
    Last    = if ($iv) { $iv.Date.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { "never" }
    Days    = $ivDays
    # Weekday ritual. Due after 2 days, overdue after 5 (a full working week missed).
    Status  = if ($ivDays -ge 5) { "OVERDUE" } elseif ($ivDays -ge 2) { "DUE" } else { "OK" }
    Why     = "distils the workday into atomic permanent notes; SecondBrain\Notes\ is fed by nothing else"
}

# --- weekly-review: Friday close-of-week synthesis ---------------------------
$wr = Get-LastRun -Path "$Vault\Inbox\weekly-review" -Filter "*.md"
$wrDays = if ($wr) { [int]($today.Date - $wr.Date).TotalDays } else { 9999 }
$isFriday = $today.DayOfWeek -eq 'Friday'
$rituals += [pscustomobject]@{
    Name    = "weekly-review"
    Command = "/weekly-review"
    Last    = if ($wr) { $wr.Date.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { "never" }
    Days    = $wrDays
    # Hard commitment since the 2026-07-17 JD restructure (Friday report cadence).
    Status  = if ($wrDays -ge 14) { "OVERDUE" } elseif ($wrDays -ge 7 -or ($isFriday -and $wrDays -ge 5)) { "DUE" } else { "OK" }
    Why     = "Friday report cadence is a standing commitment (2026-07-17 JD restructure)"
}

# --- harvest: distil shipped work into the ledger + Knowledge/ ---------------
# NOT a cadence ritual, and this is the whole design point. interview-me and
# weekly-review are due on a clock, so "days since last run" is the right signal
# for them. Harvest is due when something SHIPS and is correctly idle otherwise —
# a days-based alarm would nag through quiet weeks and stay silent on the week
# you shipped three things. So the signal is an event count, not an age.
#
# The proxy for "something shipped" is a dated entry in decisions\log.md with no
# ledger row on or after it. A locked decision is a ship event, and the gap
# between decisions recorded and ships harvested is exactly the forgotten step.
#
# Known blind spot: only catches ships that produce a decision entry. A deck
# handed to a coach or a talk given will not trigger this (the 2026-07-08 RTP
# presentation would not have). Deliberate — one precise signal beats two noisy
# ones, and a guard that cries wolf gets ignored.
$ledgerPath = "$Vault\output\_ledger.md"
$decisionsPath = Join-Path $Root "decisions/log.md"
$lastShip = $null
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ledgerPath) {
    $lastShip = Get-Content -LiteralPath $ledgerPath |
        ForEach-Object { if ($_ -match '^\|\s*(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})') { [datetime]$Matches[1] } } |
        Sort-Object -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
}

content.text:
Everything you asked for is built. It sits on 6 open PRs, which I haven't merged. The Mac-side steps can't be done from here, so they're listed below. What I checked:
- All 6 PRs exist on GitHub.
- The KeystoneOS ritual tests pass on Windows.
- The nudge script now reads your real history on Windows.
- The S2 report builds from the new data location (tested with fake data).
- The leftover worktree folders are cleaned up.

For the Parquet export I'm relying on the agent's own test results, which I didn't rerun.

## What was built

| Request | PR | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Mac backup in the evening | KeystoneOS #21 + claude-skills #8 | The backup runs at **21:00**, and its catch-up window becomes 21:00–23:59 so the 07:00 `reconcile` stops rerunning it every morning. **The CRASHBOX SSD copy only happens if the drive is plugged in at 21:00.** |
| Nudges on Windows | same two PRs | Brings back the Windows pop-up (`msg.exe`) and fixes Mac-only paths that made every ritual show "never run" on Windows. The stack doctor now expects the Windows task, and warns if the Mac copy is still running. |
| S2 on both machines | S2_Evaluation #1 | `build_report.py` reads from Drive: `04_RESEARCH/03_Active_Studies/S2_Evaluation/data` |
| Parquet export | GPS #3, Perch #1, VALD #4 | After each Mac pull, every table is written to `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/<gps\|perch\|vald>/` with a `manifest.json`. Writes are atomic. It refuses to overwrite a snapshot with fewer rows (protection against a stale copy), and a failed export never fails the pull. |

**Export caveats:**
- Two tables can legitimately shrink: GPS `positional_norms` and VALD `athlete_baselines`. After those get rebuilt, the export refuses them and alerts until you run it once with `--force`.
- VALD's `raw_tests` file is about 12 MB, re-uploaded twice a day.
- Some tests fail on Windows for reasons unrelated to this change: 14 GPS tests that need bash, and one VALD test that needs a `.env`. Run them on the Mac.

**Reading the data on Windows:**
```python
import duckdb
duckdb.sql("select * from 'G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/gps/athlete_sessions.parquet'")
```

## Run order

**1. Merge the 6 PRs.** Just say "merge them".

**2. On Windows, after merging and running `git pull` in `KeystoneOS`:**
```powershell
# Test the nudge once (a pop-up should appear):
pwsh -NoProfile -File "$HOME\Desktop\DEV\KeystoneOS\scripts\ritual-check.ps1" -Notify
# Turn the schedule on (weekdays 17:00, Fri also 15:30):
Enable-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-Rituals'
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-Rituals' | Select TaskName, State
```

**3. On the Mac, tonight, after `dev-sync`:**
```bash
# Stop the Mac nudges (Windows owns them now)
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.rituals

# Move the backup to 21:00
P=~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.dailybackup.plist
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :StartCalendarInterval" "$P"   # check the shape first
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :StartCalendarInterval:Hour 21" "$P"   # if it printed an Array, use :StartCalendarInterval:0:Hour
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :StartCalendarInterval:Minute 0" "$P"
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u) "$P"; launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) "$P"

# S2 data to Drive (one time)
DST="$HOME/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/04_RESEARCH/03_Active_Studies/S2_Evaluation/data"
mkdir -p "$DST" && rsync -av ~/DEV/S2_Evaluation/data/ "$DST/"

# First export for each source: dry run, then real
cd ~/DEV/DataBase_GPS_Reporting/gps_report && .venv/bin/python export_snapshot.py --dry-run && .venv/bin/python export_snapshot.py
cd ~/DEV/PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026 && .venv/bin/python export_snapshot.py --dry-run && .venv/bin/python export_snapshot.py
cd ~/DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem && .venv/bin/python export_snapshot.py --dry-run && .venv/bin/python export_snapshot.py
```
After tomorrow's 10:00 pull, check that `logs/last_run.json` shows `snapshot_export` ok. If it shows exit 2, macOS blocked the scheduled job from writing to Google Drive. Grant access under Privacy & Security.

## Should you schedule a nightly Windows push? Yes

Your closeout is ad hoc, and Windows has no automatic push at all (the backup script refuses to run there). So on any day you skip closeout, the Mac starts the evening with stale memory and config.

What I'd build: a Windows task around 17:30 that commits and pushes **only the context repos**: `dotclaude`, `global-memory`, `claude-memory-compiler` and SecondBrain, with a `windows auto snapshot` message. **It would leave DEV project repos alone.** Auto-committing half-finished project work onto main is worse than leaving it unpushed, and closeout stays the right tool for those. I haven't built this. Say the word and I will.

## Recommendations for a smooth switch

1. **One routine, both ends.** Start of the day on Windows: `dev-sync`. End of the day: closeout (or the 17:30 push above). Evening on the Mac: `dev-sync`. At night, the Mac pushes itself at 21:00.
2. **One owner for each database, written down.**
   - Mac: GPS, Perch and VALD, exported as Parquet.
   - Windows: nothing yet.
   - PFF: shared through snapshots.

   Never pull the same feed on both machines.
3. **Put new data in Drive or git by default.** Any new gitignored data folder is effectively stuck on one machine; S2 is the cautionary case. Point scripts at Drive with an environment-variable override, the way S2 and PFF do now.
4. **Keep databases off synced folders.** DuckDB and SQLite files go in `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows and outside `~/DEV` on the Mac, as with `PFF_DB`. Share them as Parquet, never as the database file.
5. **Fix the failing Windows AI-session backup.** It's the one broken Windows job; run `/claude-stack-doctor`.
6. **Point Perch's Windows reads at the Parquet files.** The agent found that Perch's `config.py` and `src/data.py` still read the other repos' database files on Windows, which are stale. Switching them to the snapshots is a small follow-up.
7. **Record machine ownership in one tracked file,** for example `KeystoneOS/docs/machine-ownership.md`. The two inventories from this session are the starting content. Then any session on either machine can check it instead of reconstructing it.

result: Built the evening Mac backup, Windows nudges, shared S2 data and the Parquet export for GPS, Perch and VALD across 6 open PRs (KeystoneOS #21, claude-skills #8, S2_Evaluation #1, GPS #3, Perch #1, VALD #4). Next: merge them, then run the Windows and Mac commands above.

From Eric's Windows session ("google drive migration audit"), on Eric's request (2026-09-24): please do two Mac-only tasks on this Mac, verify, and reply with results.

Context: KeystoneOS PR #21 and claude-skills PR #8 are merged. The Mac is now the evening machine, so daily-backup moves 09:00 -> 21:00 (jobs.json already says 21:00, with a makeup window of 21:00-23:59). S2_Evaluation PR #1 is merged: data/ now lives on Drive.

Step 0: `git -C ~/DEV/KeystoneOS pull`, `git -C ~/.claude/skills pull`, `git -C ~/DEV/S2_Evaluation pull`.

Task 1, move the backup to 21:00:
P=~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.dailybackup.plist
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :StartCalendarInterval" "$P"
If that prints a Dict: Set :StartCalendarInterval:Hour 21 and :StartCalendarInterval:Minute 0. If it prints an Array: use :StartCalendarInterval:0:Hour / :0:Minute.
Then: launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u) "$P"; launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) "$P"; launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.dailybackup | grep -A4 -i calendar

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# Handoff — 2026-09-24 — Windows by day, Mac by evening

## What and why

Eric is making Windows the primary daytime machine and the Mac the evening one, so that he
isn't bouncing between them. The session (Windows) started with a question about where the
Drive migration put everything. It then covered cross-machine sync, and finally built what
the day/evening split needs.

## Decisions

- **Windows = day, Mac = evening.** Everything that is text already crosses via GitHub. What was
  still stuck on one machine: the Mac's scheduled jobs and its data, plus Tier A memory.
- **Tier A memory is mirrored.** `dev-sync` runs `~/.claude/skills/dev-sync/mirror_memory.py`,
  which merges the Mac and Windows slug folders (the newer file wins; `MEMORY.md` is merged;
  nothing is deleted). First run: 53 copied, 66 replaced, 16 indexes merged. Pushed as
  dotclaude `e893618`. (claude-skills PR #7)
- **The Mac stays the only writer of GPS, Perch and VALD.** After each pull it writes Parquet
  to `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/{gps,perch,vald}/` with a `manifest.json`.
  There is a stale-writer guard (`--force` overrides). Windows reads the Parquet directly.
  (GPS #3, Perch #1, VALD #4)
- **The Mac daily-backup moves to 21:00**, with a makeup window of 21:00-23:59, so the 07:00
  reconcile doesn't re-run it. The CRASHBOX SSD capture only happens if the drive is attached
  at 21:00. (KeystoneOS #21, claude-skills #8)
- **Ritual nudges move to Windows.** `ritual-check.ps1` has its `msg.exe` branch back, with
  OS-aware paths. The stack doctor now expects `KeystoneOS-Rituals` on Windows and flags
  `com.keystone.rituals` if it is still loaded on the Mac.
- **S2 data lives on Drive:** `04_RESEARCH/03_Active_Studies/S2_Evaluation/data`.
  `build_report.py` resolves `$S2_DATA_DIR`, then Drive, then local `data/`. (S2_Evaluation #1)
  The archived originals were copied in from `08_ARCHIVE/PERSONAL/ThreeStandard/DataConsulting/S2`.
- **GPS `.pbix` is out of scope.** A colleague publishes it and holds the data.

## Mid-flight (not confirmed)

- A message was sent over Remote Control to the Mac session "forecast capture setup". It asks
  that session to (1) set the backup plist to 21:00, and (2) rsync S2 `data/` to Drive. That
  sends `ol_scores.csv` and `team_scores.csv`, which exist only on the Mac. No reply is
  possible, and it may need Eric's approval on the Mac first.

## Next actions

1. **Windows:** run `ritual-check.ps1 -Notify` once, then `Enable-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-Rituals'`.
2. **Mac:**
   - `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.rituals`
   - Confirm the backup plist says 21:00 (`launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.dailybackup`).
   - Run `export_snapshot.py --dry-run` and then for real in each of the three pull repos.
   - Check that `logs/last_run.json` has `snapshot_export` ok after the next pull.
3. **Mac:** confirm the S2 rsync ran (the folder should now include `ol_scores.csv`).
4. **Decide:** build a Windows 17:30 auto-push of the context repos only (not DEV projects).
5. **Follow-up:** point Perch's `config.py` / `src/data.py` Windows reads at the Parquet snapshots.
6. **Fix:** the Windows `Backup AI Sessions to Drive` task failed (rc=1) this morning.
   `backup-ai-sessions.ps1` has a 5-line uncommitted change from another session, committed in
   this closeout. Verify with `/claude-stack-doctor`.

## Gotchas

- Windows `git worktree remove` leaves `.git/worktrees/<name>` behind ("Permission denied").
  Clear the read-only attribute, then `Remove-Item -Force`, then `git worktree prune`.
- The auto-mode classifier blocks listing the S2 Drive data folder (athlete-named file), so
  confirm that folder by hand.
- Two snapshot tables can legitimately shrink (GPS `positional_norms`, VALD `athlete_baselines`).
  The export refuses them until it is run once with `--force`.

## Files touched

- `~/.claude/skills/dev-sync/{SKILL.md,mirror_memory.py}`, `~/.claude/skills/backup/SKILL.md`,
  `~/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor/{SKILL.md,scripts/stack-check.ps1}`
- `DEV/KeystoneOS/{data/jobs.json,scripts/ritual-check.ps1,docs/STATUS.md}`
- `DEV/S2_Evaluation/{build_report.py,AGENTS.md,docs/STATUS.md,docs/program/README_DATA.md}`
- The three pull repos: `src/snapshot.py`, `export_snapshot.py`, the pull scripts, tests, CLAUDE.md, STATUS.md
- `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/` (the mirror run)
- Drive: `04_RESEARCH/03_Active_Studies/S2_Evaluation/data/` (3 files copied from the archive)
